sanskrit: pṛthivī daṇḍo antarikṣaṃ garbho dyauḥ kaśā vidyut prakaśaḥ | madhoḥ kaśāsi ghṛtācī hiraṇyayo binduḥ ||
english: The earth is the shaft, the atmosphere the womb, the sky the lash, lightning the lustre. Thou art the lash of honey, dripping ghee, the golden drop.

sanskrit: urvy asi prabhvy asy ambho 'si nabho 'si maho 'si | ambho mā kṛṇu nabho māṃ kṛṇu maho mā kṛṇu ||
english: Thou art vast, thou art eminent, thou art water, thou art sky, thou art great. Make me water, make me sky, make me great.

sanskrit: samudro 'sy akṣito aparimitaḥ sahasrasaniḥ sahasraṃ mā gacchatu | yo vai madhukaśāyāḥ sapta madhūni veda sapta madhumatīn ||
english: Thou art the ocean, undiminished, unbounded, winning thousands — let a thousand come to me. Whosoever truly knows the seven honeys of the honey-lash, and the seven honey-bearing ones —

sanskrit: madhumantaṃ lokaṃ jayati madhv asyāhāryaṃ bhavati | yad vīdhre stanayati prajāpatir eva tat prajābhyaḥ prādur bhavati ||
english: — he wins the honey-rich world; the honey thereof becomes unassailable. When it thunders in the cloud-rift, it is Prajāpati himself who manifests thereby for his creatures.

sanskrit: tasmāt prācīnopavītas tiṣṭhet prajāpate 'nu mā budhyasveti | anv enaṃ prajāpatir anu prajā budhyante ya evaṃ veda ||
english: Therefore one should stand with the sacred cord worn to the east, saying: 'O Prajāpati, be thou aware of me.' Prajāpati becomes aware of him, and his creatures become aware of him — so knows he who thus knows.

sanskrit: yāṃ kalpayanti vahatau vadhūm iva viśvarūpāṃ hastakṛtāṃ cikitsavaḥ | sārād etv apa nudāma enān ||
english: That which skilled healers fashion as a bride at the wedding procession — all-formed, wrought by hand — let us drive them away from the very core.

sanskrit: śīrṣaṇvatīṃ payasvatīṃ karṇinīṃ kṛtāṃ kṛtyākṛtā saṃbhṛtāṃ viśvarūpām | pratyak prati pra hiṇmasi yaś cakāra tam ṛcchatu ||
english: The sorcery-effigy endowed with a head, full of sap, possessed of ears, fashioned and assembled by the sorcerer, all-formed — back and away we dispatch it; let it reach the one who made it.

sanskrit: śūdrakṛtā rājakṛtā strīkṛtā brahmabhiḥ kṛtā | jāyā patyā nutteva kartāraṃ bandhum ṛcchatu ||
english: Whether made by a Śūdra, made by a king, made by a woman, or made by brahmin-sages — like a wife repulsed by her husband, let it reach the maker, its own kinsman.

sanskrit: anayāham oṣadhyety ekā ||
english: With this herb — just this one — do I act.

sanskrit: kṛtyāḥ santu kṛtyākṛte śapathāḥ śapathīvne | pratyak prati pra hiṇmasi yaś cakāra tam ṛcchatu ||
english: Let the sorceries fall upon the sorcery-maker, the curses upon the curser. Back and away we dispatch them; let them reach the one who made them.

sanskrit: pratīcīna āṅgiraso 'dhyakṣo naḥ purohitaḥ | pratīcīḥ kṛtyā ākṛtya- -amuṃ kṛtyākṛtaṃ jahi ||
english: The westward-facing Āṅgirasa is our overseer and domestic priest. Turn back the sorceries westward, and smite that sorcery-maker.

sanskrit: yas tvovāca parehīti pratikūlam udāyyam | taṃ kṛtye 'bhi ni vartasva māsmān iccho anāgasaḥ ||
english: He who told thee 'Go forth!' in a contrary and hostile utterance — turn back upon him, O sorcery; do not seek us who are guiltless.

sanskrit: yas te parūṃṣi saṃdadhau rathasyeva vibhur dhiyā | taṃ gaccha tatra te +'yanam ajñātas te 'yaṃ janaḥ ||
english: He who fitted together thy joints with skill, as a master does with a chariot — go to him; there is thy path; this person here is unknown to thee.

sanskrit: ye tvā kṛtyā ālebhire vidvalā abhicāriṇaḥ | vidmedaṃ kṛtyādūṣaṇaṃ prativartma punaḥsaraṃ tena tvā snapayāmasi ||
english: Those knowing sorcerers who have smeared thee upon the sorcery-image — we know this sorcery-bane, the return-path counter-charm; with it we bathe thee.

sanskrit: yad durbhagāṃ prasnapitāṃ mṛtavatsām upeyima | apaitu sarvaṃ mat pāpaṃ draviṇaṃ mopa tiṣṭhatu ||
english: If we have approached a woman ill-fated, bathed in misfortune, whose calf is dead — let all evil depart from me; let no wealth fail to abide with me.

sanskrit: yat te pitṛbhyo dadato yajñe vā nāma jagṛhuḥ | saṃdeśyāt sarvasmāt pāpād imā muñcantu tvauṣadhīḥ ||
english: Whatever name they seized of thine — whether when giving to the Fathers or at the sacrifice — from all that pollution, from every sin, may these herbs release thee.

sanskrit: devainasāt pitryān nāmagrāhāt saṃdeśyād abhiniṣkṛtāt | muñcantu tvā vīrudho vīryeṇa brahmaṇa ṛgbhiḥ payasa ṛṣīṇām ||
english: From divine sin, from ancestral name-seizure, from pollution fully contracted — may the plants release thee by their power, by the brahman, by the ṛk-verses, by the milk of the sages.

sanskrit: yathā vātaś cyāvayati bhūmyā reṇum antarikṣāc cābhram | evāsmat sarvaṃ durbhūtaṃ brahmanuttam apāyati ||
english: As the wind dislodges the dust from the earth and the cloud from the atmosphere — even so let all ill-being depart from us, driven away by the brahman.

sanskrit: apa krāma nānadatī vinaddhā gardabhīva | kartṝn nakṣasveto nuttā brahmaṇā vīryāvatā ||
english: Depart, O thou braying and bound one, like a she-ass. Seek out the makers from here, driven away, expelled by the mighty brahman.

sanskrit: ayaṃ panthāpi nayāmi tvā kṛtye prahitāṃ prati tvā pra hiṇmaḥ | tenābhi yāhi bhuñjaty anasvatīva vāhinī viśvarūpā kurūṭinī ||
english: This is the path — along it I lead thee, O sorcery; we dispatch thee back toward the one who sent thee. Travel along it as a all-formed, misshapen draught-animal travels without a cart — go, consuming.

sanskrit: parāk te jyotir apathaṃ te arvāg anyatrāsmad ayanā kṛṇuṣva | pareṇehi navatiṃ nāvyā ati durgā srotyā mā kṣaniṣṭhāḥ parehi ||
english: Thy light faces away, thy path faces backward; make thy course elsewhere, not toward us. Cross beyond the ninety navigable streams, pass over the difficult crossings and the swirling rapids — harm us not; be gone.

sanskrit: vāta iva vṛkṣaṃ ni mṛṇīhi pādaya mā gām aśvaṃ puruṣam uc chiṣa eṣām | kartṝn nivṛtyetaḥ kṛtye aprajāstvāya bodhaya ||
english: Like wind crushing and felling a tree — crush and fell them; spare the cow, the horse, the man of these folk. O sorcery, turning back from here, rouse the makers to childlessness.

sanskrit: yāṃ te cakrur barhiṣi yāṃ śmaśāne kṛtyāṃ kṣetre valagaṃ vā nicakhnuḥ | agnau vā tvā gārhapatye 'bhiceruḥ pākaṃ santaṃ dhīratarā anāgasaṃ tad ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: The sorcery they wrought for thee upon the sacrificial grass, the stake they buried against thee in the cremation-ground or in the field, or by which the more cunning ones assailed thee in the Gārhapatya fire — being innocent and simple, from all that we destroy and free thee here.

sanskrit: upāhṛtam anubuddhaṃ nikhātaṃ vairaṃ tsāry anv avidāma kartṝn | tad etu yata āgataṃ tatrāśva iva vartatāṃ hantu kṛtyākṛtaḥ prajām ||
english: The enmity brought near, tracked down, buried, the treacherous deed — we have discerned the makers. Let it return whence it came; there let it turn about like a horse; let it smite the offspring of the sorcery-maker.

sanskrit: svāyasā asayaḥ santi no gṛhe vidma te kṛtye yatidhā parūṃṣi ||
english: Iron swords there are in our house; we know, O sorcery, how many joints thou hast.
